extracted.intended_audience: artists and performers (individuals, companies, international groups) planning to bring a show to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe
extracted.subtask_short: bringing a show to the Edinburgh Fringe
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, registering, producing, promoting and managing a performance at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, from initial goal-setting through post‑festival settlements and follow-up. Covers timeline, administrative steps, marketing, legal/financial considerations, and professional development resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand what the Edinburgh Festival Fringe is (open access)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fringe is an open access arts festival: anyone who has a story to tell and a venue to perform in can put on a show here. There is no centralised selection process; the Fringe Society does not produce or select shows, invite performers or cover costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan on sourcing your own venue, negotiating terms with venues (venues choose what to programme), and covering your own production costs. Use the Fringe Society only for support, guidance and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define what Fringe success would look like to you
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask why you want to bring your show to the Fringe and make a list of clear, achievable goals (e.g., exposure, developing new material, getting reviews, finding touring opportunities, earning money, networking, working on stagecraft, having fun).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List multiple goals in order of priority (which is most important). Recognise that not all outcomes are usually achieved at once and that misjudged goals can be financially costly and negatively affect your experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a strategy to achieve your goals (before/during/after)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once goals are set, create a concrete strategy of the steps needed to achieve them, considering actions you can take before, during and after the Fringe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need help forming a strategy, use the Artist Development prep sheet to book a one-to-one with the team for bespoke advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put plans into practice via professional development and networking
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively use Fringe-provided development opportunities to upskill, learn about the industry and build networks that will help meet your goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend professional development events on Fringe Connect and at Fringe Central, review previous event recordings, use the People page on Fringe Connect to find collaborators, and book one-to-one advice with the Artist Services/Development teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start early: November–April task checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: In the months November to April, clarify aims, sign up for artist bulletins, read online guides, attend info sessions, browse previous Fringe programmes and talk to past performers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put together a preliminary budget (use the budgeting tool), research and shortlist venues (see venue guide), begin contacting venues, consider how to make your show accessible, check rights for the material you will perform (see insurance and legal section), research visas for international companies, read the marketing guide, and search for accommodation via the artist accommodation portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research venues, shortlist and negotiate slots/contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Find and research potential venues, build a shortlist and start contacting them to negotiate performance slots and contractual terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the guide to finding a venue; once a slot is negotiated, be prepared to sign a contract and to coordinate box office/payment arrangements (check venue contract for payout details). Keep the venue’s dimensions and facilities in mind when planning the show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a preliminary budget and monitor finances
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a preliminary budget early and revisit it as you finalise expenditures; be realistic about costs and potential income during the Fringe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the budgeting and finance section and the provided budgeting tool. After the festival, reconcile actual expenditures and archive financial records. Be aware of Fringe Box Office settlement timelines and payout arrangements (money may be forwarded via venues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure rights, insurance and legal obligations are in place
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that the rights for the work you intend to perform are available and fulfil any insurance and legal requirements related to presenting the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the insurance and legal section for examples of what rights and insurance might include; contact the Fringe team if unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: International company requirements: visas, FEU forms and tax
rubrics_metrics.description: International companies should research UK visa requirements and, if necessary, file FEU (Foreign Entertainers' Unit) forms with HM Revenue & Customs and complete any required tax paperwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start researching these requirements early (November–April) and file forms such as FEU when appropriate (noted in July); consult international performers’ guidance on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register your show on EdFringeware and meet registration deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: After you have secured a venue slot and signed a contract, register your show on the Fringe's online registration system (EdFringeware) and comply with registration deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the registration section for specific deadlines and details about the registration process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan and prepare marketing and printed publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Design a marketing campaign and prepare printed publicity materials well in advance of the festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the marketing your show guide for ideas and advice; consider early booking discounts for advertising in the Fringe programme and plan timing of printed materials to coincide with programme launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider early on-sale dates and booking programme advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to take part in early on-sale ticket dates and consider booking advertising space in the Fringe programme early to obtain discounted rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early on-sale opportunities start from February; programme advertising discounts are available for adverts booked earlier in the year—check advertised dates in the advertising section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Fringe programme listing to promote your show
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Fringe programme launches (June), find your show listing and use the programme link to promote your show online and on social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send your press release to the Media Office for feedback, start your social media campaign, and review your budget now that major expenditures are finalised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-tune the show to the performance space and technical facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: In the lead-up (July), refine the performance considering the exact dimensions and technical facilities of your Fringe performance space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay in regular contact with venue managers to understand technical constraints and plan staging, set, lighting and sound accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with Artist Development, Arts Industry teams and Artist Advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively seek support from Fringe teams to increase industry exposure and professional opportunities during the festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Artist Development team for advice on attracting producers, programmers and promoters; engage with the Arts Industry team to discuss connections beyond the Fringe; email the Artist Advice team for promotional assistance during August.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign up and use Fringe Connect for artist development and networking
rubrics_metrics.description: Register on Fringe Connect to access artist development resources, networking tools, People pages, and sign-ups for showcases and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fringe Connect provides year-round and on-festival opportunities; use it to find collaborators, advertise showcases, and discover workshops and seminars included with registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit music license declaration where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: If your show uses music, submit the required music license declaration form to declare usage and ensure licensing compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the music licensing section for details and complete the declaration in good time before your performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep administrative details up to date (EdFringeware contact info etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain accurate contact and administrative information in EdFringeware and any venue paperwork throughout the festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure phone/email and emergency contacts are current so organisers, venues and media can reach you; update details if anything changes during the festival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily promotion and taking advantage of on-site events during August
rubrics_metrics.description: During the festival, spend time every day promoting your show and attend relevant workshops, seminars and networking events at Fringe Central to maximise exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Browse Fringe Connect for events that match your goals; some sessions are included with registration—use them to upskill and connect with industry professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand Fringe Box Office settlements and payout arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of how Fringe Box Office settlements are processed (payments are processed at the end of September) and the possible flow of funds (payments requested to be paid to a venue will be forwarded to the venue which then pays you under your venue agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check your venue contract for details about box office payout and reconcile expected income with actual receipts after settlements are processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up with industry contacts and archive your show after the festival
rubrics_metrics.description: After the festival (September), follow up with arts industry professionals who saw your show, archive press materials and show records, and finalise actual expenditure accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain contact details through your venue or the Arts Industry Office, maintain relationships for future opportunities, file press releases and financial records, and start planning for future participation if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Fringe handbooks and downloadable resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult downloadable handbooks (Fringe Guide to Registering a Show, Fringe Sustainability Toolkit, Fringe Programme Style Guide, Fringe Fundraising Handbook) for detailed, offline information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These PDFs contain deeper guidance on registration, sustainability, programme presentation and fundraising—download and review them at your own pace to supplement online guidance.
